transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. It's nice to meet you; could you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Nice to meet you, Dr. Smith. Well, I guess what really brought me in is... well, my wife, mostly. She'll be standing there telling me about my cousin’s appointments, or, you know, coordinating his rides. Which is a whole ordeal because he lives out past the old highway, and they’ve been doing all that construction out there for months. I swear they just leave the orange cones up even when nobody's working, it backs up traffic for miles and for what? But anyway, she'll be talking about his schedule, and I’m looking right at her, making eye contact and everything, but... a minute later I realize I didn’t actually take in half of what she just said.
Does this difficulty with staying focused happen in other areas of your life as well, such as at work or when you are trying to complete tasks on your own?

Yeah, it definitely happens when I'm doing things on my own, too. Like... if I sit down to work out a catering order, or if I'm listening through a parish planning call. We do this big community dinner thing at the church, and lately they've been wanting to add more vegetarian options, which I get, but nobody actually eats the baked eggplant dish they insist on making. It just sits there getting cold in those metal chafing dishes. Those little gel fuel cans they put underneath them always smell so terrible, don't they? It always reminds me of being in a chemistry lab back in college, just that harsh chemical smell. 

But, um... right, the tasks. When I'm doing that stuff, I start off fine. I'm sitting there, ready to go. But before long, my mind just wanders off completely. I'll look down at the page and realize I have to go back over the exact same notes like I never even read them in the first place.
Looking back at your life, do you remember struggling with this same kind of difficulty staying focused when you were a child or in school?

Yeah, I do. Actually, it goes way back. Even in grade school, I remember... well, my parents used to go to those parent-teacher conferences. They always held them in November, right around Thanksgiving. My mom would always bake these incredible pumpkin pies for the school bake sale they'd run at the same time. She used actual pumpkins, not the canned stuff. It takes forever to roast them down and puree it, but the taste is just completely different. I tried making it her way once, maybe ten years ago, but I burned the crust. My oven runs hot, I think. Or maybe the seal on the door is going bad. 

But anyway, they'd come back from those conferences, and it was always the same story. The teachers would say I was a bright kid, but I was always daydreaming. I'd be looking out the window instead of at the chalkboard. And my homework... half the time I'd do it and just leave it sitting inside my desk. Those old wooden desks with the lift-up tops, you know? They were great for hiding things. I kept a whole collection of baseball cards in mine. But yeah, the teachers were always having to tap on my desk and remind me to finish my classwork. So I guess it's been happening since before I was even twelve.
Aside from the difficulty with focus, have you often felt like you are 'driven by a motor' or found it hard to sit still for long periods of time?

No, not really. I'm actually pretty content just sitting. My wife is the one who can't sit still, honestly. She's always up and doing something, wiping down the counters, rearranging the throw pillows... we have these green velvet pillows on the couch, and she insists they have to be placed exactly right or the whole room looks off. She got them at this little boutique downtown that went out of business last year. It's a shame, too, because they had the best scented candles. This one called "Fireside Ember" or something like that, it smelled just like a real wood-burning fireplace. We used to have a real fireplace in our first house, but it was so drafty in the winter. You'd sit near it and freeze unless a fire was actually going. But no, I don't feel like I have a motor running or anything. I can sit in my recliner for hours just fine.
Have you ever been told by others, or do you feel yourself, that you have a tendency to act or speak impulsively without thinking through the consequences first?

No, I don't think so. I'm usually pretty careful about what I say. Well, most of the time. My brother, on the other hand, he'll just blurt out whatever comes to his mind. He did that at our cousin's wedding a few years ago. We were all at the reception, and they had this massive ice sculpture of a swan right in the middle of the buffet table. It was huge, took up half the space where the shrimp cocktail was supposed to go. I don't even know how they got it in there without it melting, because it was mid-July and the air conditioning in that hall was struggling. You could see condensation dripping down the walls. Anyway, he made some comment about the bride's dress right to her face, something about it looking like a meringue pie. She didn't talk to him for a year after that. But me? No, I usually think before I speak. I'm not really one to just jump into things or talk without thinking.
